reviewer: automated vc-code-reviewer (sonnet), independent of the implementing execute-agent
nonBlockingFindings: M1 MEDIUM (fix before the Phase 10 public deploy; judge: NOT low): no write throttle exists on memory write routes. SESSION_CAPS bound sandbox MINTING (5/IP/day, 300/day), but one valid sandbox cookie can POST /api/runs/:id/findings (51 rows per 50-finding chunk, 128 KB body), /api/decisions (8-17 rows) or /api/runs (7 rows, new doc_hash each time) without limit. About 2,000 findings requests or 12,000 decision requests exhaust the D1 Free 100k rows-written/day budget; D1 writes then fail, session creation and every quota claim throw (F5 fail-closed), so memory writes and AI/OCR are down until 00:00 UTC, repeatable daily from one session. guard:cf forbids zones/routes so no edge WAF rule can cover it. adversarial-validation.json rules out 'mint sandboxes in a loop' and notes only a READ flood; the write-flood-within-one-sandbox scenario is missing. Fix: per-workspace daily write counter claimed in memoryCtx(write:true) (reuse quota_counter UPSERT, about 1 row per request) with a cap sized to a realistic session (e.g. 600 mutating requests/day/workspace) plus a per-workspace cap on review_run/finding rows; add the scenario to adversarial-validation.json; test it.

L1 LOW: session degrade path (routes/memory/session.ts ~L84-L86) refunds the per-IP claim when the global cap is hit, so after 300 sessions/day a single IP (with a still-fresh Turnstile pass `t` in its cookie) can loop POST /api/session at about 2 D1 rows written per call with no per-IP bound. Fix: do not refund the IP claim in the degrade branch (IP cap 5/day then returns rate_limited with no write).

L2 LOW: client-chosen strings are stored unmasked: client_op_id (<=64, audit_event), finding_ref/finding_key (<=64), and more broadly finding.anchor.blockId (<=200), detector_id (<=80), model (<=120). Judged LOW (owner's own sandbox, 30 d retention, never rendered as text, web client sends engine ids), but cheap to close: enforce ID_RE (or a safe-charset regex) on client_op_id/finding_ref in the worker (parseWith refine) and run blockId/detector_id/model through maskFree or the same charset check.

L3 LOW: demo-write-block triggers have gaps (defense in depth only; no app path reaches them): no demo_ro UPDATE trigger on review_run, counsel_answer, fund, document, analyst; no DELETE block on firm_rule, rule_evidence, analyst, fund, document, review_run, finding, finding_state, counsel_question for ws_demo. Every app write is behind memoryCtx(write:true) with a sandbox workspace (read-only 'ro' cookie gets 403 before any SQL, and a ws_demo-bound signed cookie gets 401), so not exploitable today. Fix: add the missing BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE demo triggers in a new migration 0005 (migrations are forward-only; do not edit 0002 after remote apply).

L4 LOW: rule approve/reject/revoke (routes/memory/rules.ts) insert the audit row unconditionally and never check the UPDATE's meta.changes (the decision revoke path does, via insertIfDecisionActive). A concurrent double-approve with different client_op_ids writes two rule_approved audit events for one transition. Fix: conditional audit insert (WHERE EXISTS rule in the expected status) and check changes === 0.

L5 LOW: S10 recorded 11-15 ms CPU on a worst-case 157 KB findings body (> Free 10 ms) but the server still accepts findingsChunk=50 and parses the body BEFORE verifying the cookie; the 25-finding limit is client-side only. A crafted request fails with a Worker CPU error (no state change). Fix: verify the cookie signature first (no DB) and/or lower the server-side findings cap to 25.

L6 LOW: a POST /api/session by a browser that already holds a live sandbox cookie replaces it with the 'ro' cookie when the global cap is hit, orphaning the user's own sandbox for 24 h. Fix: if the incoming cookie already carries a live w/a, return it (or skip minting) instead of degrading. Also the global 300/day cap is exhaustible by 60 IPs when TURNSTILE_SECRET is unset: Phase 10 must set it.

INFO: error `reason` slugs (stale_session, expired, bad_cookie, no_workspace, schema, storage, no_db) are an enum-only oracle on cookie/DB state; no SQL text, stack or row data leaks (handle() logs kind only, app.ts catch-all returns internal_error). GET /api/memory/health is unauthenticated and unthrottled (3 reads per call; exposes schema_version/seed_version only). seed/demo.sql is apply-once: the demo workspace delete trigger is unconditional, so a changed seed spec cannot be re-applied to a live DB (Phase 10 note: fresh DB or a new migration). spend_ledger has no retention (by design, tiny rows). The comment in memory/seed-copy.ts 'Nobody ever holds a cookie bound to ws_demo' is slightly inaccurate: the read-only a='ro' cookie reads ws_demo (never writes).

VACUITY NOTES (non-blocking): the workspace_id statement lint in memory-no-cross-firm-or-workspace only regex-matches the substring `workspace_id` in each statement (it cannot prove the BOUND value comes from the cookie); the GLOBAL-map lint only checks a table name appears. Behavioural isolation tests (A/B sessions, composite FK, ws_demo cookie 401) carry the real proof. demo-workspace-not-polluted covers decision/audit/workspace triggers only, which is why L3 went unnoticed.

Execute-agent self-notes resolved: (1) unmasked client ids = L2, LOW, accepted with the cheap fix above; (2) no per-minute limiter = escalated to M1 because the abuse vector is WRITES within one session, not reads; (3) S10 CPU = L5; (4) revoke response maps 'revoked' to 'rejected': acceptable, documented deviation.
notes: Independent STRIDE + production-readiness review of phase 04b. Verified by reading all in-scope source (migrations 0001-0004, seed, db/, memory/, platform/, routes/memory/, app.ts, index.ts, wrangler.jsonc) and re-running the suite: `pnpm --filter @aduin/worker test` = 45 files / 405 tests passed; one-token runs of s05-quota-claim-atomicity (6), triggers (5), demo-workspace-not-polluted (4), idempotent-replay (2), breaker-persist (3), stale-cookie-invalid-session (3), memory-no-cross-firm-or-workspace (5) all passed; `pnpm seed:check` OK. Confirmed: every repo/platform statement binds workspace_id from the verified cookie via ?1 (only global tables ai_cache/quota_counter/spend_ledger/app_meta and purge statements are unscoped, and they carry no tenant data); no client input is interpolated into SQL (all prepare() calls use constant statement maps, lint-enforced); composite PK/FK on every child table (rule_evidence, finding_state, counsel_*, finding, document, review_run, decision supersedes/answer/analyst) make cross-workspace links impossible, origin_* and audit entity_id are provenance-only plain columns written from the verified workspace; ws_demo is unreachable for writes (liveness requires kind='sandbox' so a signed ws_demo cookie is 401; the a='ro' cookie has no w and write routes throw read_only_demo before any SQL; demo triggers block decision/audit/workspace writes outside seed_mode); append-only triggers on decision/audit/answer with DELETE allowed only while workspace.status='purging' (set and cleared inside one atomic purge batch, never externally visible); quota claim is a single guarded UPSERT...RETURNING (cap-safe, no row = refused, any D1 error throws per F5); breaker sets the in-isolate trip first then persists, tripped() throws on read error (F14); RulesPort is built per request from the cookie workspace and reads only status='active'; idempotent replay via UNIQUE(workspace_id, client_op_id) with the audit row first in the atomic batch returns the stored result for the same action and 400 op_reused otherwise; privacy: detail_json is hard-coded NULL on findings, snippets are masked before the 300-char slice, decision note/fund/doc labels/rule text/interpretations all pass maskFree, audit detail_json holds ids/enums only; guards: x-aduin-client header, strict same-origin Origin + sec-fetch-site on every mutation, JSON content-type, content-length plus streamed body cap (64 KB, 128 KB findings), 401 for missing/forged/stale/expired/purging sessions; INDEXED BY uq_decision_active is correct (the queries carry the literal status='active' that implies the partial index predicate, and explain-lookup asserts it); purge never touches ws_demo (kind='sandbox' filter plus CHECK), is child-first and atomic, and the cron failure is non-fatal. No critical or high findings. The one finding that must not be forgotten is M1 (write-flood availability), which cannot be mitigated at the edge under the guard:cf no-zone rule; it should be fixed in code before the Phase 10 deploy (cheap, in the 04b blast radius) or explicitly accepted by the orchestrator with a Phase 10 precondition. Evidence pack: risk-gate.json, context-snippets.json, verification.json, adversarial-validation.json present; this review-decision.json now present; adversarial-validation.json needs the M1 scenario added.
rationale: Tenant isolation, append-only integrity, demo protection, quota/breaker fail-closed behaviour and privacy handling all hold under independent review with passing tests; the only substantive gap is availability (no write throttle within one sandbox) which is Medium for a free-tier demo with no data-compromise path and is fixable cheaply, so the decision is approve-with-fixes and auto-stop is cleared (no high or critical findings).
